headline: ‘You only need to be human to seek justice,’ says Inqilab Moncho’s Abdullah Al Jaber
cardTitle: To seek justice, you only need to be human!
standfirst: The convener of the platform founded by slain activist Sharif Osman Hadi says demands for justice — for Shakil, for 28 October and for July — should not depend on party lines.
keyPoints: Inqilab Moncho convener Abdullah Al Jaber says seeking justice for killings should not require party membership.
He named the murder of Chhatra Dal leader Shakil, the 28 October 2006 Paltan violence and the July 2024 killings.
The message was shared by the platform’s “March for Insaf” campaign under #JusticeForHadi.

paragraphs: Abdullah Al Jaber, convener of Inqilab Moncho, has said that demanding justice for political killings in Bangladesh should not depend on which party a person supports.

“I don’t need to be BNP to demand justice for Shakil’s murder. Today, I don’t need to be Jamaat to demand justice for the 28 October ‘logi-boitha’ carnage. I don’t need to be NCP to demand justice for the July killings. To demand justice for all these killings, you only have to be human,” he said, in a message shared by the platform’s March for Insaf campaign.

sections.heading: Three cases, three parties
paragraphs: Md Shakil Islam, 30, a joint general secretary of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) in Natore’s Gurudaspur upazila, was hacked by helmeted attackers on 14 October and died in hospital 12 days later. Police have detained Nooruzzaman, son of BNP lawmaker Abdul Aziz of Natore-4, and a court placed him on a three-day remand on 27 October. The lawmaker has denied any link to the killing.

Jaber’s message came on the anniversary of 28 October 2006, when deadly clashes broke out in Dhaka’s Paltan area as activists were beaten with sticks and oars (logi-boitha). Jamaat-e-Islami marks the day each year. The “July killings” refers to the deaths during the July 2024 mass uprising, whose student leaders later formed the National Citizen Party (NCP).

sections.heading: What is Inqilab Moncho?
paragraphs: Inqilab Moncho is a cultural and political platform founded by Sharif Osman Hadi, a student leader who rose to prominence during the July Uprising. Hadi was shot at close range in Dhaka’s Bijoynagar on 12 December 2025 and died days later in Singapore, where he had been flown for treatment. Since then the platform has campaigned for justice over his killing.

Its current “March for Insaf” (March for Justice) began in Panchagarh on 7 October, reached Dhaka’s Shahbagh on 23 October and is set to end in Teknaf. Its demands include justice for Hadi’s killing, implementation of the July National Charter, and justice for the July, Shapla and Pilkhana killings.

socialSummary: Inqilab Moncho’s Abdullah Al Jaber says demanding justice should not depend on party lines.
